lines.text: I'd sit by a fire first.
HARVEST FAIR — Tonight on the Green. Pie judging at six. Lanterns at dusk. Music by the Weller brothers.
LOST: grey cat, answers to Biscuit (sometimes). Last seen eating somebody's butter. Apply to A. Hale, whose butter it was.
LOST: grey cat. Someone has crossed out LOST and written, in Ada Hale's hand: UNFORTUNATELY NOT.
Pinned beneath, nearly hidden: a faded card marked with a rune of three crossed lines.
The old Warden's mark. 'When the stones go cold, walk the line.' I'd forgotten that was here.
Biscuit, hm. I'd try the south road, if I'd eaten Ada's butter. I'll keep an eye out.
The awning is stiff with frost. A row of jam jars has frozen to the shelf.
Cider doughnuts, still warm. Someone has drawn a pumpkin on the price board.
Empty crates and a hand-painted sign: QUILTS — OPENING TONIGHT.
Patchwork quilts in every colour of the maples. One has a little wizard stitched in the corner.
In the big one, a square of blue wool, a square of brown corduroy and a square of grey shirting. You'd never know they'd been late.
That's a good likeness. Whoever leaded that glass had stood beside the stone itself, and didn't care to say so.

conversations._note: rummage_<n> plays when Eldwin opens his nth container in somebody's house (story/interact.ts). He may dodge, but he never lies outright.

lines.text: Forty autumns these people have trusted me with their walls. Nobody said a word about their dressers.
You do learn a town this way. Mostly who's been meaning to darn what.
If anyone asks, I was looking for frost. And I was. I looked while I was in there.
They'd give it to me if I asked. That's rather the trouble with asking.
Pa's coat, buttoned to the chin. It stands facing the church, the way it has all week.
The coat is moving. There isn't any wind.
The door is shut for now.
A small red mitten, frozen fast to the fence post.
Come here, you. Somebody's missing you.
